title: Projective complete flag scheme with its linear action
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $n\geq1$. For a commutative $k$-algebra $A$, a complete flag in $A^n$ means a sequence $0=F_0\subset F_1\subset\cdots\subset F_n=A^n$ of $A$-submodules such that, locally on $\operatorname{Spec}A$, each $F_i$ is a direct summand free of rank $i$. Scalar extension sends a flag to the images of its submodules in the extended free module. This functor of $A$ is represented by a $k$-scheme $\operatorname{Fl}_{n,k}$ [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-representable-functor]. The scheme is projective [def-pc-projective-morphism], proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over $k$. There is a $k$-scheme action of $\operatorname{GL}_{n,k}$ [def-sc-general-linear-group] on $\operatorname{Fl}_{n,k}$ whose action on every algebra's points is $g\cdot(F_i)_i=(gF_i)_i$. The action is associative and has identity acting trivially. Its $k$-points are exactly complete flags of $k$-linear subspaces in $k^n$.

source.place: Propositions 7.29--7.30 and preceding flag functor, printed p.146; the natural GL action is the action on flags in the quotient construction. Properness and finite type are included in completeness of this projective algebraic scheme.

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$. For $1\leq i\leq n$ apply lem-sfb-free-quotient-grassmann-projective with $(N,r)=(n,n-i)$, obtaining $G_i$ and its universal quotient $q_i:\mathcal O_{G_i}^n\twoheadrightarrow Q_i$. Let $K_i=\ker(q_i)$. Locally trivialize $Q_i$ and lift its finitely many basis sections; after shrinking these lifts give a right inverse of $q_i$. Thus the quotient sequence splits locally. On such an affine open, use lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction to identify modules and quasi-coherent sheaves. Then $K_i$ is a direct summand of a finite free module, hence has a free-open cover by lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover; its rank is $i$, since a split decomposition into free modules has ranks adding to $n$ after passage to any residue field. In particular $K_n=\mathcal O^n$ because $Q_n=0$. Pullback of a split decomposition remains a split decomposition: in local coordinates it is the same inclusion and projection matrices with coefficients mapped to the new ring. Consequently the pullback of $K_i$ is the kernel of the pulled-back quotient under EVERY base change; no flatness hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Proposition 7.30, Grassmannian input; quotient convention from Stacks constructions.tex Tag 089T (lemma-gkn-representable).

proof.text: Form $P=\prod_{i=1}^n G_i$ over $S$ using def-pc-fibre-product, and denote the pulled-back universal quotients and kernels again by $Q_i,K_i$. For $1\leq i<n$ let $d_i:K_i\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_P^n\twoheadrightarrow Q_{i+1}$, and put $d=\bigoplus_{i=1}^{n-1}d_i:\bigoplus K_i\to\bigoplus Q_{i+1}$. Both bundles are finite locally free by step 1. On an affine open where they are free, lem-sc-affine-free-map-zero-locus gives a closed subscheme, locally of finite presentation, representing the condition that the pulled-back $d$ is zero. This condition restricts to opens and is local on the test scheme: a sheaf morphism is zero exactly when all its restrictions on an open cover are zero. Hence lem-sc-local-closed-locus-gluing applies, producing a closed immersion $c:Z\hookrightarrow P$ such that $h:T\to P$ factors through $Z$ exactly when $h^*d=0$. A direct sum of these maps is zero exactly when every $h^*d_i$ is zero. When $n=1$ these sums are zero bundles, the condition is vacuous, and $Z=P=S$.

source.place: Proposition 7.30, polynomial incidence conditions; scheme-theoretic implementation using the matrix-entry zero loci and gluing in Stacks perfect.tex Tag 0BDL (lemma-locally-closed-where-H0-locally-free).

proof.text: For every $S$-scheme $T$, maps $T\to P$ are tuples of the quotient classes classified by the $G_i$, by def-pc-fibre-product and lem-sfb-free-quotient-grassmann-projective. Each quotient is determined up to quotient-preserving isomorphism by its embedded kernel. By step 1 these kernels are locally direct summands of ranks $i$. Moreover $h^*d_i=0$ means precisely that $K_i$ maps into $\ker(\mathcal O_T^n\to Q_{i+1})=K_{i+1}$. Thus step 2 identifies maps $T\to Z$ bijectively with flags of locally direct summand subbundles of $\mathcal O_T^n$; append $K_0=0$. Conversely such subbundles give locally free quotients of ranks $n-i$ and therefore a map to $P$, and the inclusions give its unique factorization through $Z$. These constructions are inverse, since taking the kernel and taking the quotient by an embedded submodule are inverse on quotient classes. They commute with pullback by the local splitting calculation in step 1 and the Grassmannian's base-change clause. Set $\operatorname{Fl}_{n,k}=Z$.

source.place: Flag functor and Proposition 7.29; Proposition 7.30, incidence realization. This gives the scheme-valued version of the functor, before restricting to affine schemes.

proof.text: For $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$, the unit and quasi-coherent counit of lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction identify $A$-modules with quasi-coherent modules on $T$, and lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-free-module identifies $\widetilde{A^n}$ with $\mathcal O_T^n$. This equivalence identifies submodules and quotient classes (kernels and cokernels are characterized by their universal properties). In particular it carries a submodule locally a free direct summand of rank $i$ to exactly such a subbundle, and conversely: restriction to $D(f)$ is localization by lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections, and these opens form a basis. Therefore step 3 gives exactly the algebra-valued functor in the statement, including its embedded submodules, not merely their abstract isomorphism classes. For $A\to B$, lem-weil-pbc-tilde-pullback-base-change identifies pullback with tensoring by $B$. The split local inclusions of step 1 stay injective after tensoring, so their submodules become precisely the images in $B^n$ stipulated in the statement. Taking $A=k$, local direct summands are precisely linear subspaces of dimension $i$; these bijections give the asserted description of $k$-points.

Each $G_i$ has a closed embedding into some finite projective space by lem-sfb-free-quotient-grassmann-projective, including $G_n=S=\mathbf P^0_S$. Induct on the number $j\geq1$ of factors to embed $\prod_{i=1}^jG_i$ into a single projective space. The base case is the specified embedding of $G_1$. If the first $j$ factors embed in $\mathbf P^a_S$ and $G_{j+1}$ embeds in $\mathbf P^b_S$, the map of their product into $\mathbf P^a_S\times_S\mathbf P^b_S$ factors into two base changes of these closed immersions, hence is closed by lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change and lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp. Compose with lem-chow-segre to obtain an embedding into $\mathbf P^{(a+1)(b+1)-1}_S$. This proves the induction, with no need to equalize the projective-space dimensions. Composing the resulting embedding of $P$ with $c:Z\hookrightarrow P$ gives a closed embedding of $Z$ into finite projective space, again by the composition lemma. Thus $Z\to S$ is H-projective in def-kun-projective.

source.place: Proposition 7.30, final product/closed-subvariety argument; Stacks constructions.tex Tag 01WD (lemma-segre-embedding).

proof.text: By lem-kun-projective-implies-proper applied to the embedding of step 5, $Z\to S$ is proper. By def-weil-proper-morphism this includes finite type, and by def-weil-finite-type-morphism finite type includes quasi-compactness. Thus the embedding of step 5 together with quasi-compactness proves projectivity also in the statement's def-pc-projective-morphism convention. This proves all three geometric properties without imposing smoothness, algebraic closedness, or a restriction on the characteristic.

source.place: Proposition 7.30 (projective, hence complete), with Stacks morphisms.tex Tag 01WC (lemma-locally-projective-proper).

proof.text: Put $H=\operatorname{GL}_{n,k}\times_S Z$ using def-pc-fibre-product. The first projection supplies an invertible matrix $g$ of global functions on $H$, by the coordinates and inverted determinant in def-sc-general-linear-group. Pull the universal flag on $Z$ back along the second projection. The submodules $gK_i\subseteq\mathcal O_H^n$ are again a flag of locally free direct summands of ranks $i$: applying an invertible matrix to a local basis and its complement produces such a basis and complement for the image. Step 3 therefore supplies a unique morphism $a:H\to Z$ classifying this flag. Pulling this construction to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ yields exactly $(g,(F_i))\mapsto(gF_i)$, by the naturality proved in steps 3--4 and the algebra-points formula in def-sc-general-linear-group. Thus the asserted action on every algebra's points is induced by a scheme morphism, rather than only by a pointwise set action.

source.place: Proposition 7.29 and preceding flag functor: the natural action by change of frame; expanded using the universal flag.

proof.text: On $\operatorname{GL}_{n,k}\times_S\operatorname{GL}_{n,k}\times_S Z$, the pullback of the flag along $a\circ(m\times1)$ is $((gh)K_i)_i$, while that along $a\circ(1\times a)$ is $(g(hK_i))_i$. The multiplication formula in def-sc-general-linear-group gives equality as embedded submodules, since $(gh)v=g(hv)$. The injectivity of the classification bijection of step 3 therefore makes the two morphisms equal. Pulling back along the identity section gives $(1K_i)_i=(K_i)_i$, so the same uniqueness proves $a\circ(e\times1)=\mathrm{id}_Z$. These are the associativity and identity diagrams of a scheme action. The calculation holds on these universal test schemes, not just on field-valued points, so it proves the scheme equalities in arbitrary characteristic and over nonreduced algebras as well.

source.place: Proposition 7.29, natural GL action on the flag functor; multiplication and identity laws checked on the universal flags.

Checked against Milne iAG2017 printed p.146 (the flag functor, Props 7.29-7.30), which the statement matches; not a target node, no SGA. All 8 steps hold against the full statements of the 20 cited nodes. (1) The Grassmannian G_S(n,n-i) quotient splits locally, its kernel is locally free of rank i by the free-cover node, and the kernel commutes with every base change because the sequence is split. (2) The zero locus of the sum of the maps K_i->Q_{i+1} is glued; the gluing node's restriction, locality and local-locus hypotheses were checked through the composition isomorphism of def-pc-module-pullback. (3)-(4) Flags are classified over all schemes, then over algebras by the tilde equivalence, localization on D(f) and theta for scalar extension; k-points are flags of k^n. (5) The product of the Grassmannians embeds by an induction with base and step, using two base changes of closed immersions and Segre with possibly different dimensions. (6) H-projective gives proper, hence finite type, hence quasi-compact, so projective in the def-pc convention. (7)-(8) The GL action comes from the universal invertible matrix on GLxZ; associativity and unit follow from the m^* and epsilon formulas and the uniqueness of step 3. Edge cases checked: n=1, A=0, any characteristic, non-flat extension. The grep -R search found no duplicate. lem-sfb-solvable-subgroup-flag-realization has a special-case clause (F algebraically closed, no action); advisory: that node could cite this item. Accepted tool_uses: the free-cover, zero-locus, gluing, tilde-pullback, Segre and projective-implies-proper nodes, all generic off-unit tools on the Milne route. No changes.

lean.statement: theorem exists_completeLinearFlagScheme (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) : ∃ (Fl : Over (Spec (.of k))) (e : ∀ A : CommAlgCat.{u} k, ((yoneda.obj Fl).obj (op ((algSpec (.of k)).obj (op A)))) ≃ CompleteLinearFlag A n) (a : ModObj (GeneralLinearGroup (LinearGroupSchemes.Index.{u} n) k) Fl), IsProjective Fl.hom ∧ IsProper Fl.hom ∧ (LocallyOfFiniteType Fl.hom ∧ QuasiCompact Fl.hom) ∧ (∀ (A B : CommAlgCat.{u} k) (f : A ⟶ B) (x : (algSpec (.of k)).obj (op A) ⟶ Fl) (i : Fin (n + 1)), ((e B ((algSpec (.of k)).map f.op ≫ x)).step i).toSubmodule = completeFlagScalarImage f.hom.toRingHom ((e A x).step i).toSubmodule) ∧ (∀ (A : CommAlgCat.{u} k) (g : (algSpec (.of k)).obj (op A) ⟶ GeneralLinearGroup (LinearGroupSchemes.Index.{u} n) k) (x : (algSpec (.of k)).obj (op A) ⟶ Fl) (i : Fin (n + 1)), ((e A (CartesianMonoidalCategory.lift g x ≫ a.smul)).step i).toSubmodule = (((e A x).step i).toSubmodule).map (GeneralLinearGroup.homMulEquiv (LinearGroupSchemes.Index.{u} n) k A g).val.mulVecLin) ∧ (∀ F : Fin (n + 1) → Submodule k (LinearGroupSchemes.Index.{u} n → k), (Monotone F ∧ F 0 = ⊥ ∧ F (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ i, Module.finrank k (F i) = i.val) ↔ ∃! x : (algSpec (.of k)).obj (op (CommAlgCat.of k k)) ⟶ Fl, ∀ i, ((e (CommAlgCat.of k k) x).step i).toSubmodule = F i)
